name: Reed McGinley-Stempel
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stytch (now a Twilio subsidiary)
profile: Co-founded passwordless authentication company Stytch in 2020 with Julianna Lamb after both worked at Plaid; Stytch became a unicorn and grew into a B2C/B2B identity platform for humans and AI agents. Twilio announced its acquisition of Stytch on Oct 30, 2025; the deal closed in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Twilio bought Stytch in late 2025 to build an 'intelligent identity layer' for agentic AI; Stytch's changelog confirms Twilio is now its parent company.
deep_cut_fact: He and Julianna Lamb met at Plaid working on bank-account authentication, where they saw how much engineering time went into auth flows that were never the product; Stytch launched with just email magic links.
notes: Hurun unicorn-founder identity (Stytch) is clear, but the SEC link to Omega Flex (OFLX) as director/10% owner could not be verified (EDGAR full-text search shows no filings under his name; Omega Flex's major holders are the Reed family). Likely a record-merge error; the net worth figure tied to OFLX may not be his.

name: Dennis H Nelson
current_role: President & CEO, The Buckle, Inc. (NYSE: BKE), Kearney, Nebraska
profile: Lifelong Buckle executive who joined the Kearney, Nebraska denim and apparel retailer as a part-time salesman in 1970 and rose to president (1991) and CEO (1997). His wealth comes from his long-held Buckle shares; he still runs the company, which operates hundreds of stores across the US.
interesting_fact: He is a true 'stockroom to corner office' CEO: he started as a part-time salesman at the Brass Buckle while a student and has spent his entire career at the company.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 he was named the first-ever College of Business and Technology Distinguished Alumnus at UNK (Kearney State College, business administration '73); the dean credited him with the decision to expand The Buckle beyond its original Kearney store.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Company route via Buckle IR / corporate office in Kearney, NE.

name: Rohit Gyanchandani
current_role: Director, RSPL Group (maker of Ghadi detergent), Kanpur, India
profile: Second-generation director of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, the family FMCG conglomerate behind Ghadi, one of India's best-selling detergent brands, founded in 1988 by his father's generation (Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani). Alongside brother Rahul he helps run the group, reportedly focusing on international markets and hygiene/personal-care brands.
interesting_fact: Energy angle: RSPL has 15 solar plants totalling about 50.1 MW and built a ₹40bn+ soda-ash plant in Devbhumi Dwarka, Gujarat (commissioned FY2019-20) to backward-integrate its detergent supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: The group was originally incorporated in Kanpur in 1988 as 'Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd.' (later renamed RSPL Ltd.); a predecessor company merged in 2006 was named 'Rohit Soaps & Detergents Pvt. Ltd.'
notes: Family is famously low-profile ('silent billionaires'). He was quoted as Director in RSPL's 50-year anniversary release (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/spotlight/news-wire/from-kanpur-to-global-rspl-group-celebrates-50-years-contributing-to-india-s-growth-story). The division-of-responsibility detail comes from a Wikipedia mirror, so treat it as indicative. The deep-cut fact doesn't say the company was named after him, so don't present it that way.

name: James E Flynn
current_role: Managing Partner, Deerfield Management (healthcare investment firm, New York)
profile: Healthcare investor who joined Deerfield Management in 2000 as a pharma specialist and has run the firm since founder Arnold Snider retired in 2005. He expanded Deerfield beyond its hedge-fund roots into structured financings, drug-discovery partnerships with academic centers, and the Cure life-sciences campus at 345 Park Avenue South. Through Deerfield he is a director/10% holder of Nuvalent and other biotechs.
interesting_fact: Deerfield runs CURE, a life-sciences innovation campus at 345 Park Avenue South in Manhattan; Flynn has talked about a 'Lab of the Future' that automates molecule-building and could bring that work back to New York from abroad.
deep_cut_fact: He studied cellular & molecular biology and economics at the University of Michigan and began his career as a specialty-pharma analyst at Kidder, Peabody (1988-93), then did corporate development at Alpharma before Furman Selz. He chaired the quality committee of Continuum Health Partners' board.
notes: Deerfield's contact page lists Jessica Sagers for communications inquiries and Karen Heidelberger (karenh1@deerfield.com) for partnership inquiries. Possible podcast angle: building a healthcare-innovation real-estate and data ecosystem in NYC.

name: Sujay U Desai
current_role: Listed director/CEO of Frost International Ltd (Kanpur/Mumbai commodity trading firm), now in insolvency proceedings (CIRP)
profile: Promoter-director of Frost International, a Kanpur-linked merchant trading company led by his father Uday Desai. He appeared on the Hurun India list in 2017. The company is now reportedly in India's corporate insolvency resolution process.
notes: DUE-DILIGENCE FLAG: In Jan 2020 the CBI booked Frost International and its directors, including Sujay Desai, over an alleged Rs 3,592-crore fraud on a 14-bank consortium led by Bank of India. Not a suitable outreach target; no contacts collected.

name: Todd C Davis
current_role: CEO, Ligand Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: LGND); director of Pelthos Therapeutics and Palvella Therapeutics
profile: Healthcare royalty investor who co-founded Cowen Healthcare Royalty Partners (now HealthCare Royalty) in 2006 and later founded RoyaltyRx Capital (2018). A long-time Ligand board member, he became CEO in December 2022 and has refocused Ligand on its royalty-aggregator model of funding late-stage drugs in exchange for royalties.
interesting_fact: He helped pioneer pharmaceutical royalty investing as an asset class: he co-founded Cowen Healthcare Royalty Partners in 2006, then ran it as managing partner until 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Navy veteran and US Naval Academy graduate who began his business career in sales and marketing at Abbott Laboratories before earning a Harvard MBA and moving to Apax Partners.
notes: Best route is Ligand investor relations. The navy detail comes from a board-news aggregator quoting Ligand's Dec 2022 press release.

name: Arnaud Ajdler
current_role: Founder, Managing Partner & Portfolio Manager, Engine Capital (activist investment firm, New York); director, UniFirst
profile: Belgian-born activist investor who was a partner at Crescendo Partners before founding Engine Capital in 2013. Engine runs about $1.2-1.7bn and has pushed for change at companies such as Lyft, UniFirst and Avantor. Through Engine he has been a 10% holder of Civeo, which runs workforce accommodation for energy and mining sites, and of Orthofix.
interesting_fact: He trained as an aerospace engineer before becoming an activist investor: B.S. in mechanical engineering from the Free University of Brussels and an S.M. in aeronautics from MIT, then a Harvard MBA.
deep_cut_fact: While at Crescendo Partners he taught as an Adjunct Associate Professor of Business at Columbia Business School.
notes: Engine Capital's contact page lists the general-inquiries email (mdiagonale@) and the investor-inquiries email (apessolano@). Energy angle: Civeo stake (oil-sands and mining workforce lodging).
